text:
For years, Jenkins built every merge we shipped without much complaint, but it wasn't in good shape. Our setup had grown into a tangle of plugins, hand-tuned agents, and pipeline definitions that only a few people felt confident touching. Builds were slow, the bill kept climbing, and keeping the server running had become a job of its own.

So we moved our CI to GitHub Actions. Over three weeks we migrated all 41 pipelines, rewriting each one as a workflow that lives next to the code it builds. It went better than we expected. Builds now take 6 minutes instead of 14, so developers get feedback in less than half the time. Our monthly CI bill fell from $900 to $410, which saves us almost $6,000 a year.

Below, we explain why we left Jenkins and how we ran the migration without slowing development. We also cover what tripped us up and what we'd do differently next time.
